main_issue: How to pay for soft drinks (and whether the alcohol-spent house fund was fair) now that the fund is empty

A-B.evidence: A accepts B's point about soft drinks (T3) but they never settle payment; A defends the alcohol spend (T9, T11) while B asks how to pay (T12).

A-C.evidence: C questions the alcohol cost and fund (T5, T7) and A answers (T6); C later accepts D's view (T15) while A stays defensive (T11). No shared arrangement.

A-D.evidence: D says spending the fund on alcohol is unfair (T8, T10); A defends it (T9, T11); D wants drinkers to cover soft drinks (T16), and A never agrees.

B-C.evidence: C says the fund can't be used and tells B so (T7), and proposes everyone chip in $10 (T13) in response to B's question (T12), but C then withdraws it (T15) and B never endorses a plan.

B-D.evidence: B wants soft drinks bought and asks how to pay (T12); D proposes drinkers cover them (T16). They are compatible, but B never responds.

C-D.evidence: D rejects C's $10 each plan as unfair (T14); C concedes 'You're right' and asks D for a fair way (T15); D proposes drinkers pay (T16).
